display.purpose: The home hero, 'Start Value Calculator', gradient-clipped. One per screen.

headline.purpose: The Start Value readout — the hero metric. tabular-nums, gradient-clipped, animated on change.

title.purpose: Modal and component titles, skill names, the routine-name input.

body.purpose: The default — skill names, descriptions, row content. Sans.

label.purpose: Mono, uppercase, tracking-wider. Section headers, code numbers, stat labels, all machine-readable data.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Modals and picker dialogs (shadow-2xl). Separates an overlay from the page.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Event/skill cards on hover (shadow-xl shadow-black/40), paired with a -4px translate.

shadows.name: hover-lift-tinted
shadows.purpose: Skill cards on hover (shadow-lg shadow-sky-900/20) — a faint sky-tinted lift.

motion.name: spring-toast
motion.purpose: Toast entrance (180ms) — a slight overshoot for a pop-in feel.

motion.name: ease-out-standard
motion.purpose: Fade (140ms) and count-up (220ms) — default for appearing/changing content.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: transition-colors / transition-all on buttons, chips, cards, hover lifts.

motion.name: duration-progress
motion.purpose: Element-group progress-bar fill width transition (transition-all duration-300).

containers.name: score-rail
containers.purpose: Fixed-width Start Value breakdown rail on desktop.

keyframes.name: toast-in
keyframes.value: from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(8px) scale(0.96); } to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0) scale(1); }

keyframes.name: count-up
keyframes.value: from { opacity: 0.4; transform: translateY(-4px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
keyframes.purpose: Start Value number re-animates on every change, 220ms ease-out.

atmosphere.bodyBackground: radial-gradient(at 20% 0%, rgba(56,189,248,0.06) 0, transparent 50%), radial-gradient(at 85% 100%, rgba(168,85,247,0.05) 0, transparent 50%)
atmosphere.purpose: A barely-there sky/violet radial wash on the slate-950 ground, background-attachment: fixed. The one decorative gesture in the system — lifts the field out of flat monochrome.
atmosphere.plannedChange: To be removed (confirmed by the design owner; not yet in code). Target: a flat slate ground (#020617) with no radial wash. Documents the current state only.

components.name: Primary Button (Save)
components.description: The one semantic-positive action. Emerald fill, disables when there's nothing to save.

components.name: Invert Button (modal confirm)
components.description: The bright, high-contrast primary action inside a modal; same styling drives the active filter chip.
components.css: .ds-btn-invert { background: #f1f5f9; color: #0f172a; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 6px 12px; border: none; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s; } .ds-btn-invert:hover { background: #ffffff; } .ds-btn-invert:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: New / Cancel / Custom — the neutral action.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: #1e293b; color: #e2e8f0; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 6px 12px; border: none; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #334155; }

components.name: Add-Skill Button (dashed)

components.css: .ds-btn-add { width: 100%; background: transparent; color: #94a3b8; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; padding: 10px; border: 1px dashed #334155; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.2s; } .ds-btn-add:hover { border-color: rgba(14,165,233,0.6); color: #7dd3fc; background: rgba(14,165,233,0.05); }

components.name: Event Pill (header nav, active)
components.description: Header navigation pill in its event identity color (shown: PH / sky). Inactive pills are slate-800.
components.css: .ds-chip-event { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; background: rgba(14,165,233,0.2); color: #bae6fd; border: 1px solid rgba(14,165,233,0.4); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(14,165,233,0.4); transition: background 0.2s; } .ds-chip-ico { width: 16px; height: 16px; }

components.name: Search Input
components.description: Fill-is-the-field input. No resting border; a single ring on focus.

components.name: EG Badge
components.description: Atomic element-group data chip (shown: EG III / violet). Mono, bordered, color-coded by group.
components.css: .ds-badge-eg { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 2.5rem; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 4px; background: rgba(124,58,237,0.3); color: #ddd6fe; border: 1px solid rgba(124,58,237,0.5); }

components.name: Difficulty Badge
components.description: Atomic difficulty chip (shown: D / yellow-600) on the fixed A→J heat scale, numeric value in mono.

components.description: The signature hero: gradient-washed panel with the Start Value as a large tabular gradient-clipped readout. components.name: Panel Card

narrative.overview: The D-Score Calculator is a dark, dense scoring instrument for people who already speak gymnastics. It reads like a well-made judging console: a near-black slate ground, flat panels layered by tone rather than shadow, and a single large tabular readout — the Start Value — that is the hero of every screen. Everything is legible at a glance and citeable to the Code of Points. Nothing is ornamental; the one decorative gesture in the whole system is a barely-there radial wash of sky and violet behind the darkest surfaces, just enough to lift the field out of flat monochrome. Color is rationed. The slate neutral ramp carries 90% of every screen, and the vivid hues earn their place by meaning something: emerald is credit, amber is caution, rose is loss, sky is the primary signal. The six events each own one identity color — a 'lit apparatus' accent at the 300-level of its hue — and those colors appear only where event identity is the point. The typographic signature is a terminal-style monospace used for every label, code identification number, and numeric value: it makes the whole surface feel measured and instrument-grade, and it visually separates data (mono) from prose (sans). Density and speed outrank hand-holding. This is a tool for a fluent audience composing and optimizing routines, often one-handed on a phone on the gym floor. The anti-reference is the cheerful, rounded, pastel 'fitness app'. Precision is the personality.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black slate ground (#020617) with flat, tone-layered panels — depth without shadow.
One hero metric per screen: the Start Value as a large tabular-nums gradient readout.
A terminal-monospace label system that marks everything machine-readable (codes, values, groups).
Color used only semantically or for event identity — never as decoration.
Six event identity colors, each the 300-level of its hue, used sparingly as 'channel' accents.

rules.name: The Rationed Color Rule
rules.body: Slate carries the screen. A vivid hue appears only when it means something — credit, caution, loss, signal, or which apparatus you're on. If a color is doing decoration, remove it.

rules.name: The Alpha-Over-Slate Rule
rules.body: Build surfaces and states by compositing color over slate at low alpha (bg-sky-500/10, border-emerald-600/60, surface at /40), not with solid fills. Solid, fully-saturated fills are reserved for small badges, toasts, and the Save button.

rules.name: The Twelve-Grade Difficulty Scale
rules.body: Difficulty badges (A→J) run a fixed heat spectrum: A slate → B blue → C emerald → D yellow → E orange → F red → G purple → H pink → I fuchsia → J deep-fuchsia. This mapping is normative; never recolor a difficulty badge off this scale.

rules.name: The Mono-Data Rule
rules.body: Every code identification number, difficulty value, Start Value, bonus figure, and classification label is set in monospace with tabular-nums where it's numeric. Prose and names stay sans. Never set a routine description or a sentence in mono, and never set a score in the proportional sans.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Label Rule
rules.body: Section and group labels are small, uppercase, mono, tracking-wider, and text-slate-400/-500. They name a region without competing with its content.

rules.name: The Fixed-Rail Rule
rules.body: On desktop the Start Value breakdown is a fixed-width rail that never reflows as the routine grows; the routine list absorbs all width change. On mobile it stacks below, never into a cramped side-by-side.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: No surface carries a shadow at rest. Depth at rest is conveyed by tonal layering (alpha slate over canvas). Shadow is reserved for overlays and hover/active response.

rules.name: The Hairline-Border Rule
rules.body: Every panel gets a 1px border (slate-800 at rest, slate-700 for emphasis, a semantic hue at alpha for state). Because the system is shadowless at rest, the border is the edge — never ship a borderless card on the canvas.

dos: Do keep slate as ~90% of every screen and let a vivid hue appear only when it carries meaning (credit = emerald, caution = amber, loss = rose, signal = sky, identity = event color).
Do set all codes, values, and classification labels in monospace with tabular-nums for numbers; keep prose and names in the sans. Data is mono, prose is sans — always.
Do build surfaces by compositing color over slate at low alpha (/10–/60), and give every panel a 1px border since the system is shadowless at rest.
Do make the Start Value the single hero of any screen it appears on — large, tabular, gradient-clipped, animated on change.
Do stack the builder's two panes to one column below md; the breakdown goes under the builder, never into a cramped phone-width split.
donts: Don't add resting shadows. Depth at rest is tonal layering; shadow means overlay or hover.
Don't recolor a difficulty badge off the A→J heat scale, or restyle an event away from its assigned identity hue.
Don't use color decoratively — no gradient-as-ornament beyond the established hero/radial washes, no colored surface that isn't signalling state or identity.
Don't introduce a web font or set data in the proportional sans; the system/mono split is the typographic identity.
Don't soften the product toward a friendly consumer-fitness look (pastel fills, big rounded illustrations, explanatory hand-holding). The audience is fluent; precision is the personality.
